world.title: India jails two youth protest leaders for entering closed protest site
world.summary: On Wednesday, an Indian court ordered Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das held in judicial custody for five days after they climbed barricades to enter Delhi’s Jantar Mantar protest site, which police had recently closed to demonstrations. The court released a third activist, Ajinkya Shind
world.content: On Wednesday, an Indian court ordered Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) leaders Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das held in judicial custody for five days after they climbed barricades to enter Delhi’s Jantar Mantar protest site, which police had recently closed to demonstrations. The court released a third activist, Ajinkya Shinde, on a personal bond. The CJP and opposition groups are demanding Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation over a voter-roll revision that removed more than 130 million names. Opposition parties allege the changes could benefit Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s BJP; the Election Commission denies favouring any party and says people wrongly removed can re-enrol. The arrests followed a weekend security crackdown in Delhi, where police detained thousands of people and blocked a planned protest. Authorities removed Jantar Mantar from the list of designated protest sites and named three alternatives. Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi condemned the jail terms; Ranka and Das can seek bail from a higher court.

world.title: Ukrainian drone strikes hit three Yandex data centers, disrupting services
world.summary: Ukrainian drone strikes hit three Yandex data centers in Russia over four days, taking the Sasovo and Vladimir facilities offline and damaging part of the Kaluga facility. Yandex serves millions of consumers and hundreds of thousands of businesses; its services and outside companies that rely on its cloud infrastructur
world.content: Ukrainian drone strikes hit three Yandex data centers in Russia over four days, taking the Sasovo and Vladimir facilities offline and damaging part of the Kaluga facility. Yandex serves millions of consumers and hundreds of thousands of businesses; its services and outside companies that rely on its cloud infrastructure experienced outages. Disruptions affected taxi bookings, maps, email, cloud files and Yandex Pay. Users reported trouble accessing funds, and businesses were unable to access hosted data. Service problems were also reported in Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan, Armenia and Belarus, where companies and customers rely on Yandex infrastructure. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the strikes were a response to Russian attacks on Ukrainian data centers. His claim that the strikes also reduced Russian social-media disinformation remains unsubstantiated: researchers said available Cloudflare data measured automated web traffic, including search-engine crawlers, rather than social-media activity. Yandex said its cloud platform was operating in emergency mode and advised customers to activate alternative recovery plans; Russian media reported that repairs could take months.
world.image_alt: Ukrainian drone strikes hit three Yandex data centers, disrupting services

world.title: Russia holds Japanese newspaper reporter in pre-trial custody on espionage charges
world.summary: Russia has detained Yuki Imai, a reporter for Japan’s Hokkaido Shimbun, and a Moscow court ordered him held in pre-trial custody until Dec. 12 on espionage charges. The FSB alleges that, acting on instructions from Japanese intelligence, he collected information about Russia’s military capabilities and the number of Ku
world.content: Russia has detained Yuki Imai, a reporter for Japan’s Hokkaido Shimbun, and a Moscow court ordered him held in pre-trial custody until Dec. 12 on espionage charges. The FSB alleges that, acting on instructions from Japanese intelligence, he collected information about Russia’s military capabilities and the number of Kuril Islands residents mobilized or volunteering to fight in Ukraine. The allegations have not been tested in court. A conviction under Article 276 of Russia’s Criminal Code can carry a sentence of up to 20 years. Japanese officials say they are seeking information about the arrest and have asked Russia to ensure humanitarian consideration and fair treatment. The Hokkaido Shimbun said it was confirming details and that the reporter’s safety was its top priority. Japan has imposed sanctions on Russia over its war in Ukraine, and the two countries dispute sovereignty over the Kuril Islands. Imai’s pre-trial detention is scheduled to end Dec. 12, according to Russian media reports.
world.image_alt: Russia holds Japanese newspaper reporter in pre-trial custody on espionage charges

world.title: French student protests draw 161,500 over school conditions
world.summary: Tens of thousands marched across France on Tuesday, Oct. 13, in support of high school students demanding better classroom conditions. The Interior Ministry counted 161,500 participants, while unions put the figure at 480,000. The fifth nationwide day of protests included demonstrations in Paris and other cities. Clash
world.content: Tens of thousands marched across France on Tuesday, Oct. 13, in support of high school students demanding better classroom conditions. The Interior Ministry counted 161,500 participants, while unions put the figure at 480,000. The fifth nationwide day of protests included demonstrations in Paris and other cities. Clashes broke out on the fringes of the Paris marches, where police used tear gas and water cannons. Students cite teacher shortages, deteriorating school buildings and overcrowded schedules. The government has pledged to provide 3,000 substitute teachers for the 114 most affected high schools, but students have dismissed the measure as insufficient. The movement began in September and has drawn support from unions, university students and climate activist Greta Thunberg. The Education Ministry said 147 school staff had been injured since the protests began. Police have taken more than 6,800 people into custody, according to the Justice Ministry. Student groups and unions are expected to join wider cost-of-living demonstrations on Saturday, Oct. 17. The education minister is due to meet student organizations on Thursday.
world.image_alt: French student protests draw 161,500 over school conditions

world.title: Bipartisan senators demand Trump revoke Russian diesel sanctions waiver
world.summary: A bipartisan group of 12 U.S. senators urged President Donald Trump on Oct. 13 to abandon his Russian diesel arrangement and rescind the Treasury Department’s sanctions waiver, calling the move a betrayal of Ukraine and U.S. allies. Six Republicans and six Democrats signed the letter, which said the deal would do littl
world.content: A bipartisan group of 12 U.S. senators urged President Donald Trump on Oct. 13 to abandon his Russian diesel arrangement and rescind the Treasury Department’s sanctions waiver, calling the move a betrayal of Ukraine and U.S. allies. Six Republicans and six Democrats signed the letter, which said the deal would do little to lower fuel costs while giving Moscow revenue to support its war. Trump defended the arrangement on Tuesday, saying the diesel was intended for global markets, not specifically for the United States, and arguing that additional supply could ease high prices. The senators countered that the arrangement would offer “limited to no relief” to Americans and help Russia deepen security cooperation with China, Iran and North Korea. A 2022 law bars most Russian energy imports. A sanctions law Trump signed last month authorizes economic pressure on Russia and countries that support its war effort; the senators urged him to use that law instead.
world.image_alt: Bipartisan senators demand Trump revoke Russian diesel sanctions waiver

world.title: German court opens first Nord Stream sabotage trial of Ukrainian ex-officer
world.summary: A court in Hamburg opened the first trial over the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline blasts on Oct. 14, with former Ukrainian officer Serhii K. accused of helping lead the operation. Prosecutors allege he and a team of divers, an explosives expert and a boat captain attacked civilian energy infrastructure on orders from uniden
world.content: A court in Hamburg opened the first trial over the 2022 Nord Stream pipeline blasts on Oct. 14, with former Ukrainian officer Serhii K. accused of helping lead the operation. Prosecutors allege he and a team of divers, an explosives expert and a boat captain attacked civilian energy infrastructure on orders from unidentified Ukrainian state agencies. Serhii K. denies involvement. The indictment charges him with causing an explosion, damaging property, disrupting public services and complicity in a war crime. Prosecutors say the alleged aim was to permanently halt gas deliveries and prevent Russia from earning revenue to fund its war. The charges remain allegations, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has denied Ukraine’s involvement. The German government has declined to comment, citing the independent judicial process. Sixteen hearings are scheduled through Dec. 17, with further sessions planned for January and February 2027. No verdict date has been announced.
world.image_alt: German court opens first Nord Stream sabotage trial of Ukrainian ex-officer

world.title: MI5 warns Iran targets British military sites as Russia expands hybrid warfare
world.summary: MI5 chief Ken McCallum warned in London on Oct. 13 that Iran is seeking to target more heavily protected sites, including military installations, while Russia is intensifying hybrid operations against Britain and other Ukraine allies. He said MI5 had recorded more than 50 arrests in Iran-linked operations over the past
world.content: MI5 chief Ken McCallum warned in London on Oct. 13 that Iran is seeking to target more heavily protected sites, including military installations, while Russia is intensifying hybrid operations against Britain and other Ukraine allies. He said MI5 had recorded more than 50 arrests in Iran-linked operations over the past year. State threats had quadrupled in a decade, he said, and the agency now devotes more resources to them than during the Cold War. The warning followed a suspected plot near RAF Fairford. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Iran was highly likely to have been involved and that the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps had almost certainly directed the plot. McCallum declined to discuss the active investigation but said the incident was “not unique”; Iran denies involvement. McCallum also warned that terrorists were using AI to improve reconnaissance and attack methods. He said AI’s potential to enable biological weapons or new pathogens was a particular concern, though such misuse has not yet occurred. He described Russia as the leading state aggressor and cited alleged cyber and sabotage activity in Europe; Moscow denies involvement in hostile operations.
world.image_alt: MI5 warns Iran targets British military sites as Russia expands hybrid warfare

world.title: Saudi OpenAI engineer charged after recorder found in executive conference room
world.summary: A 35-year-old Saudi national who worked as an OpenAI engineer was arrested on Oct. 9 and charged with trying to intercept oral communications after investigators said he planted a recording device in a San Francisco executive conference room. He appeared in federal court on Oct. 13. The charge does not establish guilt.
world.content: A 35-year-old Saudi national who worked as an OpenAI engineer was arrested on Oct. 9 and charged with trying to intercept oral communications after investigators said he planted a recording device in a San Francisco executive conference room. He appeared in federal court on Oct. 13. The charge does not establish guilt. OpenAI employees found the device on Sept. 30, plugged into a USB port behind a television and concealed in toilet paper. Prosecutors said it had been installed around Sept. 28. The room was used for discussions of confidential research, product plans and business strategy. OpenAI said it found no indication that the employee improperly accessed or took model weights, source code or customer data. Prosecutors also cited a second, similar device found in a bag linked to the employee and surveillance footage showing him returning to the room. The FBI investigation continues, and Alfozan is due back in court on Oct. 19 for a detention hearing.
world.image_alt: Saudi OpenAI engineer charged after recorder found in executive conference room

business.title: CVS agrees to $315 million settlement in federal opioid case
business.summary: CVS Pharmacy and several subsidiaries agreed to pay $315 million to resolve a U.S. Justice Department lawsuit alleging they filled medically unnecessary prescriptions for opioids and other controlled substances. The settlement also requires CVS to add safeguards to ensure such prescriptions are filled only when medical
business.content: CVS Pharmacy and several subsidiaries agreed to pay $315 million to resolve a U.S. Justice Department lawsuit alleging they filled medically unnecessary prescriptions for opioids and other controlled substances. The settlement also requires CVS to add safeguards to ensure such prescriptions are filled only when medically appropriate, Justice Department officials said. The 2024 lawsuit alleged CVS filled high-dose prescriptions from providers known as “pill mills” and that staffing levels, performance measures and incentive pay contributed to pharmacists filling prescriptions without verifying their legitimacy. CVS said it strongly disagreed with the claims, described its medication-safety programs as “best-in-class” and said the settlement includes no admission of wrongdoing.
business.image_alt: CVS agrees to $315 million settlement in federal opioid case

business.title: ASML lifts 2026 forecast to €44 billion–€45 billion on AI demand
business.summary: ASML raised its 2026 revenue forecast to €44 billion–€45 billion after third-quarter sales rose to a record €11.66 billion and net profit nearly doubled to €4.96 billion. The Dutch chip-equipment maker said customers are raising their near- and medium-term demand forecasts based on expectations for the scale and durati
business.content: ASML raised its 2026 revenue forecast to €44 billion–€45 billion after third-quarter sales rose to a record €11.66 billion and net profit nearly doubled to €4.96 billion. The Dutch chip-equipment maker said customers are raising their near- and medium-term demand forecasts based on expectations for the scale and duration of AI investment. ASML expects demand to exceed its planned equipment supply in both 2027 and 2028, and some customers are already interested in placing orders for 2029 and 2030. The company is looking at ways to further expand capacity in 2028. For the current quarter, it forecast revenue of €14.2 billion–€15.2 billion and a 57% gross margin.

business.title: IMF warns AI borrowing and bond yields threaten financial stability
business.summary: The International Monetary Fund warned on Oct. 13 that surging artificial-intelligence borrowing and a disorderly rise in bond yields could unsettle global markets, as technology companies increasingly compete with governments for investors’ money. The Fund said higher yields could reduce asset values, including AI-rel
business.content: The International Monetary Fund warned on Oct. 13 that surging artificial-intelligence borrowing and a disorderly rise in bond yields could unsettle global markets, as technology companies increasingly compete with governments for investors’ money. The Fund said higher yields could reduce asset values, including AI-related shares, and weaken government bonds used as collateral. It attributed current bond-market pressure mainly to energy prices, interest-rate expectations and elevated term premiums, rather than AI borrowing alone. In the IMF’s downside scenario, a sharp pullback in AI investment if expected productivity and profits fail to materialize could cut global GDP by 1.1% by 2028 and U.S. output by 1.8%. An IMF official said that outcome would be unlikely to amount to a global recession. The Fund also warned that more capable AI could increase cyber risks to financial institutions and market infrastructure. The IMF outlined the risks as finance ministers and central bank governors gathered in Bangkok for the IMF and World Bank meetings. The Fund urged governments to strengthen public finances as borrowing costs rise.
business.image_alt: IMF warns AI borrowing and bond yields threaten financial stability

business.title: Bipartisan senators urge Trump to reverse Russian diesel waiver
business.summary: Twelve senators, evenly split between Republicans and Democrats, urged President Donald Trump on Tuesday to withdraw from his agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin and rescind the Treasury waiver allowing Russian diesel into global markets. They argued the arrangement would fund Russia’s war against Ukraine w
business.content: Twelve senators, evenly split between Republicans and Democrats, urged President Donald Trump on Tuesday to withdraw from his agreement with Russian President Vladimir Putin and rescind the Treasury waiver allowing Russian diesel into global markets. They argued the arrangement would fund Russia’s war against Ukraine while offering Americans little relief from high fuel prices. Trump defended the decision, saying the fuel was intended for the world market, not the United States, which he said had been affected by high prices and damaged refineries. The senators countered that the added supply would have a negligible effect on prices and that Russian revenue would support Moscow’s war effort and security ties with China, Iran and North Korea. Legal scholars cited by TIME said the 2022 import ban requires advance consultation and certification before the prohibition can be lifted. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has defended the administration’s legal authority. Most provisions of a separate Russia sanctions law are scheduled to take effect Oct. 18, and Treasury’s temporary license runs through April 7, 2027.
business.image_alt: Bipartisan senators urge Trump to reverse Russian diesel waiver

business.title: U.S. banks lift third-quarter profits as rate and inflation risks mount
business.summary: JPMorgan Chase, Citigroup, Wells Fargo and Goldman Sachs reported higher third-quarter profits than a year earlier, but JPMorgan missed analysts’ estimates as rising expenses and weaker fixed-income trading offset growth elsewhere. The banks reported continued consumer spending and business investment and warned that h
business.content: JPMorgan Chase, Citigroup, Wells Fargo and Goldman Sachs reported higher third-quarter profits than a year earlier, but JPMorgan missed analysts’ estimates as rising expenses and weaker fixed-income trading offset growth elsewhere. The banks reported continued consumer spending and business investment and warned that higher rates and persistent inflation could pressure consumers and the economy. JPMorgan earned $15.3 billion, or $5.57 a share, below the $5.93 analysts expected; its expenses rose 12%, and a $658 million securities loss reduced earnings. Goldman’s profit rose to $5.29 billion, while Citigroup’s increased 40% and Wells Fargo earned $5.95 billion. Banks also reported loan and deposit growth but faced higher costs to retain deposits as customers sought better returns. Bank of America and Morgan Stanley were due to report on Oct. 14.
business.image_alt: U.S. banks lift third-quarter profits as rate and inflation risks mount

business.title: Anthropic warns AI worms could turn smart devices into botnets by 2026
business.summary: Anthropic warned that small artificial-intelligence models could be months away from copying themselves across internet-connected home devices, potentially forming networks that are difficult to shut down. Its researchers said the capability could arrive by the end of 2026 if models continue to improve, but stressed th
business.content: Anthropic warned that small artificial-intelligence models could be months away from copying themselves across internet-connected home devices, potentially forming networks that are difficult to shut down. Its researchers said the capability could arrive by the end of 2026 if models continue to improve, but stressed that no fully autonomous rogue replicator is known to exist. Anthropic said appliances and cameras often have weaker security protections, while a distributed infection could operate without a single control point. Tests showed replication in simplified environments, not autonomous spread through commercial data centers. Anthropic said future systems could target those more powerful computers.
business.image_alt: Anthropic warns AI worms could turn smart devices into botnets by 2026

business.title: Six Flags shares fall 16% after fatal coaster accident prompts closures
business.summary: Six Flags Entertainment shares fell as much as 16.3% on Tuesday after a man died and several people were injured in an incident at Six Flags Over Georgia near Atlanta. Police identified the man as Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, 42. Witnesses said he was ejected from a coaster. Witnesses and local reports identified it as Gol
business.content: Six Flags Entertainment shares fell as much as 16.3% on Tuesday after a man died and several people were injured in an incident at Six Flags Over Georgia near Atlanta. Police identified the man as Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, 42. Witnesses said he was ejected from a coaster. Witnesses and local reports identified it as Goliath, though officials did not confirm which coaster was involved. The company temporarily closed nine similar coasters across six parks in the United States and Canada, including rides in California, Illinois, New Jersey, Ohio, North Carolina and Ontario. The company has not announced a reopening date, and Cobb County police are investigating. Shares traded at $9.98 after falling 16.3% in early trading, extending a decline that began in September. The stock was down 33.8% for the year, according to CBS News. Georgia’s Office of Insurance and Safety Fire Commissioner said it was conducting a comprehensive review, and coaster manufacturer Bolliger & Mabillard said it was investigating.
business.image_alt: Six Flags shares fall 16% after fatal coaster accident prompts closures

business.title: France says cyberattacks affected 700 supermarkets; Dutch grocer systems disrupted
business.summary: France’s finance minister told Parliament on Tuesday that cyberattacks had affected about 700 of the country’s 10,000 supermarkets, as authorities investigated refrigeration failures at grocery chains. Roland Lescure said food supplies were not at risk but described the attack as touching “the heart of our food securit
business.content: France’s finance minister told Parliament on Tuesday that cyberattacks had affected about 700 of the country’s 10,000 supermarkets, as authorities investigated refrigeration failures at grocery chains. Roland Lescure said food supplies were not at risk but described the attack as touching “the heart of our food security”. The Paris prosecutor’s cybercrime unit is investigating the damage, including spoiled stock and reports of fires. Coopérative U said 80 of its 2,000 stores were affected; most avoided refrigeration disruptions, though some discarded food. Danfoss, whose equipment was used in affected stores, said most compromised systems were older models that no longer received software or security updates. Separately, Dutch retailer Ahold Delhaize took some systems offline after a security issue, disrupting websites and online services at several of its brands while stores remained open. The company said it had no evidence that customer or employee data had been stolen. No connection between its incident and the French refrigeration attack has been established. Investigators have not confirmed whether previously disclosed Danfoss vulnerabilities were exploited.
business.image_alt: France says cyberattacks affected 700 supermarkets; Dutch grocer systems disrupted

science.title: DNA recorder maps mouse embryo cell lineages through 13.5 days
science.summary: Researchers used a DNA-based recording system to reconstruct cell lineages in a developing mouse embryo, tracking development from the fertilized egg’s first division through day 13.5. The study, published Oct. 8 in Science, offers a way to examine how cells’ early ancestry relates to their later roles in forming organ
science.content: Researchers used a DNA-based recording system to reconstruct cell lineages in a developing mouse embryo, tracking development from the fertilized egg’s first division through day 13.5. The study, published Oct. 8 in Science, offers a way to examine how cells’ early ancestry relates to their later roles in forming organs and tissues. The recording captured a mark distinguishing the embryo’s first two cells. One cell produced more descendants, but both contributed to diverse cell types in nearly equal proportions. The researchers also found that different cell types committed to their roles at different times. The team focused its detailed analysis on one embryo whose recording preserved the most extensive history.
science.image_alt: DNA recorder maps mouse embryo cell lineages through 13.5 days

science.title: Study finds elephant carcasses shape ecosystems for up to a decade
science.summary: A study links nutrients left by elephant “megacarcasses” to areas with lower biodiversity but greater ecosystem activity. The study suggests that a carcass can have different ecological effects within the same landscape rather than simply increasing biodiversity. The Washington Post reports that an elephant’s body can
science.content: A study links nutrients left by elephant “megacarcasses” to areas with lower biodiversity but greater ecosystem activity. The study suggests that a carcass can have different ecological effects within the same landscape rather than simply increasing biodiversity. The Washington Post reports that an elephant’s body can leave a mark on the landscape for a decade. The research examines the long-lasting effects of nutrients left behind after elephants die.
science.image_alt: Study finds elephant carcasses shape ecosystems for up to a decade

science.title: Webb traces record-setting fast radio burst to young dwarf galaxy
science.summary: Astronomers traced fast radio burst FRB 20240304B to a small, actively star-forming dwarf galaxy after detecting the brief signal with South Africa’s MeerKAT radio telescope and identifying its host with the James Webb Space Telescope. The burst travelled for about 10 billion years and was emitted when the universe was
science.content: Astronomers traced fast radio burst FRB 20240304B to a small, actively star-forming dwarf galaxy after detecting the brief signal with South Africa’s MeerKAT radio telescope and identifying its host with the James Webb Space Telescope. The burst travelled for about 10 billion years and was emitted when the universe was roughly 3 billion years old. The host galaxy was about 1,000 times less massive than researchers expected, and most of its stars may have formed within the past 30 million years. That recent, vigorous star formation makes a magnetar—an intensely magnetic neutron star formed from a massive young star—a plausible source, although astronomers say the cause of fast radio bursts remains uncertain. The burst’s path also revealed evidence of intervening cosmic structures, including a possible previously unknown galaxy group about 3.5 billion light-years away.
science.image_alt: Webb traces record-setting fast radio burst to young dwarf galaxy

science.title: Creatine protected hippocampal neurons in rats with chronic colitis
science.summary: Creatine supplementation prevented several signs of hippocampal damage in rats with chronic colitis, including inflammation and altered neuron activity, according to a study published in *Brain, Behavior, and Immunity*. Colitis had more pronounced effects in male rats, which showed neuron loss and electrical changes; f
science.content: Creatine supplementation prevented several signs of hippocampal damage in rats with chronic colitis, including inflammation and altered neuron activity, according to a study published in *Brain, Behavior, and Immunity*. Colitis had more pronounced effects in male rats, which showed neuron loss and electrical changes; females had inflammation but less functional damage. The researchers gave the animals creatine before inducing colitis and throughout the experiment. The findings have not been tested in people and do not establish that creatine protects the brains of people with inflammatory bowel disease.
science.image_alt: Creatine protected hippocampal neurons in rats with chronic colitis

science.title: Timekeepers prepare to vote on ending leap seconds over risks to digital systems
science.summary: The 69 member states of the International Bureau of Weights and Measures are due to vote on Oct. 15 in Versailles, France, on ending leap seconds. If approved, the change would take effect in May 2027. Timekeepers have added 27 leap seconds since 1972 to keep atomic-clock time aligned with Earth’s irregular rotation, b
science.content: The 69 member states of the International Bureau of Weights and Measures are due to vote on Oct. 15 in Versailles, France, on ending leap seconds. If approved, the change would take effect in May 2027. Timekeepers have added 27 leap seconds since 1972 to keep atomic-clock time aligned with Earth’s irregular rotation, but the corrections can disrupt computer and communications systems. The proposal would let the gap between atomic time and Earth-rotation time grow instead of making periodic one-second adjustments. Timekeepers say a negative leap second—subtracting a second—could become necessary as Earth’s rotation speeds up in the near term. The estimated probability is 30% by 2035, and critical-infrastructure operators are described as largely unprepared. Under the proposed limit, the difference could reach one hour only after more than 3,000 years.
science.image_alt: Timekeepers prepare to vote on ending leap seconds over risks to digital systems

science.title: Anthropic warns AI worms could spread through smart-home devices
science.summary: Anthropic researchers warned that small AI models could soon self-replicate across internet-connected household devices, spreading through smart TVs, cameras and appliances without human direction. The researchers said the threat could be months away if AI models continue improving, but said they have not built a fully
science.content: Anthropic researchers warned that small AI models could soon self-replicate across internet-connected household devices, spreading through smart TVs, cameras and appliances without human direction. The researchers said the threat could be months away if AI models continue improving, but said they have not built a fully self-replicating system. Unlike conventional malware, an AI worm could use a lightweight model to identify unfamiliar devices and run on the computing power of compromised gadgets rather than relying on a data center. Such devices are often inexpensive and poorly secured, the researchers said. Their estimate is rough: it draws on one type of gadget and a past botnet, and the worm could take days to copy itself. With no central switch to shut down a distributed infection, containment could be difficult.
science.image_alt: Anthropic warns AI worms could spread through smart-home devices

science.title: FAA reviews SpaceX plan for 456 annual Starship launches
science.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration is reviewing SpaceX’s proposal for up to 456 Starship launches a year at its Starbase facility in South Texas. The agency is preparing an environmental review and holding public consultations on the expansion. The proposal would increase annual launches from 25 to 456. The review wil
science.content: The Federal Aviation Administration is reviewing SpaceX’s proposal for up to 456 Starship launches a year at its Starbase facility in South Texas. The agency is preparing an environmental review and holding public consultations on the expansion. The proposal would increase annual launches from 25 to 456. The review will assess potential effects on air quality, wildlife and air traffic. SpaceX’s plan also calls for up to 912 landings annually at the site.
science.image_alt: FAA reviews SpaceX plan for 456 annual Starship launches

science.title: SpaceX sends 6,300 pounds of science cargo to space station
science.summary: SpaceX launched its CRS-35 cargo mission from Cape Canaveral, Florida, on Oct. 13, sending a Dragon spacecraft with more than 6,300 pounds of research materials, equipment and crew supplies to the International Space Station. The capsule is scheduled to dock autonomously with the station on Oct. 15. The experiments inc
science.content: SpaceX launched its CRS-35 cargo mission from Cape Canaveral, Florida, on Oct. 13, sending a Dragon spacecraft with more than 6,300 pounds of research materials, equipment and crew supplies to the International Space Station. The capsule is scheduled to dock autonomously with the station on Oct. 15. The experiments include human tissue models to study brain and heart health and aging in microgravity, alongside research on plant health and drug-resistant organisms. A separate protein-crystallization experiment will grow crystals of a target protein with a drug-candidate compound so researchers can examine how the compound binds to the protein and use the findings in structure-based drug design. The Dragon also carries the station’s final pair of roll-out solar arrays, part of an upgrade to offset declining output from its original arrays. NASA says the new arrays will be installed during spacewalks later in October and early November.
science.image_alt: SpaceX sends 6,300 pounds of science cargo to space station

sports.title: McIlroy backs LIV golfers’ return as league faces October 25 deadline
sports.summary: Rory McIlroy said he would support LIV Golf players returning to the PGA Tour, arguing their presence could boost the tour’s business as the breakaway league seeks enough player commitments to relaunch. Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi on October 13, he said LIV is no longer a threat to establis
sports.content: Rory McIlroy said he would support LIV Golf players returning to the PGA Tour, arguing their presence could boost the tour’s business as the breakaway league seeks enough player commitments to relaunch. Speaking at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi on October 13, he said LIV is no longer a threat to established tours. LIV’s proposed $300 million financing depends on securing enough player commitments by October 25. Jon Rahm has rejected the terms, and only Richard Bland and Cameron Tringale had publicly committed, the Associated Press reported. The DP World Tour says players who sign for LIV’s 2027 season cannot be members, while the PGA Tour bars departing LIV players for a year after their last event. McIlroy favors readmission but says existing members’ views should count.
sports.image_alt: McIlroy backs LIV golfers’ return as league faces October 25 deadline

sports.title: England recall Bethell and call up teenage Rew for Australia
sports.summary: England have recalled Jacob Bethell after a knee injury and given teenage wicketkeeper-batter Thomas Rew and fast bowler Eddie Jack their first international call-ups for the white-ball tour of Australia. Jofra Archer also returns for the three-match ODI series, while Rew and Jack are among the young players selected f
sports.content: England have recalled Jacob Bethell after a knee injury and given teenage wicketkeeper-batter Thomas Rew and fast bowler Eddie Jack their first international call-ups for the white-ball tour of Australia. Jofra Archer also returns for the three-match ODI series, while Rew and Jack are among the young players selected for the five-match T20 series. Harry Brook will captain both squads. The ODIs begin in Perth on November 13, with England close to full strength as they prepare for next year’s World Cup in southern Africa. England will rotate players for the T20 series, leaving out frontline quicks Archer, Gus Atkinson, Josh Tongue and Sonny Baker, along with Ben Duckett, as those players prepare for the Test tour of South Africa. The final T20 is scheduled for Canberra on December 2.
sports.image_alt: England recall Bethell and call up teenage Rew for Australia

sports.title: Maresca defends City
sports.summary: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca defended his players’ exuberant celebrations after their 3-0 win at Liverpool, asking critics, “What do you want us to do?” Sunday’s victory at Anfield was City’s first match since an independent commission found the club guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules. City deny
sports.content: Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca defended his players’ exuberant celebrations after their 3-0 win at Liverpool, asking critics, “What do you want us to do?” Sunday’s victory at Anfield was City’s first match since an independent commission found the club guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules. City deny wrongdoing and have appealed. Erling Haaland, Jeremy Doku and Rayan Cherki scored, and City players celebrated with their travelling supporters after the final whistle. The celebrations drew criticism following the commission’s verdict. Liverpool fans had jeered City during the match. Maresca said the team remained focused on winning matches. Captain Ruben Dias said the squad had discussed the verdict and remained calm. City were due to host Champions League holders Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday, October 14. The appeal hearing was expected to conclude by mid-December under the league’s current rules.

sports.title: English football regulator warns clubs face collapse without reforms

The draft State of the Game report says rising debt and dependence on owner funding leave clubs vulnera
sports.content: England’s Independent Football Regulator warned that clubs across the top five divisions face serious financial risks, with 94% reporting losses in 2025-26 despite the game generating more than £9 billion in revenue. The draft State of the Game report says rising debt and dependence on owner funding leave clubs vulnerable: 66% could not survive 90 days without new owner support, while 29% could not last 30 days. The watchdog called for clubs to strengthen financial risk management and contingency planning, and urged reform of revenue distribution between the Premier League and lower divisions. The Premier League and EFL have yet to agree on a new funding settlement. Regulator chair David Kogan said a deal was close, while the regulator warned it could intervene if football fails to reach an agreement. The draft report will undergo an eight-week public consultation, with the final report due in early 2027.

sports.content: The Los Angeles Dodgers will start Shohei Ohtani at designated hitter in Wednesday’s National League Championship Series Game 3 against Milwaukee, manager Dave Roberts said Tuesday, after discussing whether the injured star needed rest. The Dodgers trail the Brewers 2-0 in the best-of-seven series and return to Los Angeles needing a win to avoid moving within one loss of elimination. Ohtani is 3-for-20 with three singles, seven strikeouts and no extra-base hits this postseason; he has not homered since Aug. 18. He has been managing left-knee and right-biceps problems but said his symptoms have eased and he continues to adjust his swing. Roberts said Ohtani believes he is well enough to contribute and is close to making mechanical adjustments. Ohtani is expected to bat between second and sixth against Brewers left-hander Robert Gasser, while Blake Snell is set to start for Los Angeles. The four-time MVP remains in a lineup that produced only nine singles and one double in the first two games.

sports.content: David Kogan, chair of English football’s Independent Football Regulator (IFR), says he will resign if politicians try to influence how the watchdog handles Manchester City’s case. City is appealing an independent commission’s finding that it breached Premier League financial rules over nine seasons, from 2009 to 2018; the club denies wrongdoing. The IFR can assess whether owners, directors and senior executives are fit to run clubs and could ultimately force an owner to sell. Kogan says the regulator will wait until the appeal process ends before deciding whether to use its statutory powers. A separate sanctions hearing could take months to convene, and City can appeal any punishment. Kogan spoke at the launch of the IFR’s first State of the Game report, which found that most English clubs made a loss in 2025-26. The regulator plans to begin issuing club licences in November, and Kogan said it would consider any verdict after appeal in its licensing decisions.

He said football authorities would make the final decision and urged people to
sports.content: Paris Saint-Germain coach Luis Enrique said Manchester City deserved the trophies they won on the pitch and should not be stripped of them, speaking Tuesday before PSG’s Champions League visit to the Etihad Stadium on Wednesday, October 14. He said football authorities would make the final decision and urged people to wait for the process to conclude. An independent Premier League commission found City guilty of 114 of 115 alleged breaches of financial rules covering 2009 to 2018; City denies wrongdoing and has appealed. Possible sanctions include fines, points deductions, relegation or removal of titles won during that period, but no sanction has yet been announced. On Wednesday, Enzo Maresca’s City face the reigning back-to-back European champions. Maresca has won all eight matches in all competitions since taking over, while former City manager Pep Guardiola is expected to return to the Etihad.

sports.summary: Arsenal scored three times in seven second-half minutes to beat Lille 3-0 at the Emirates Stadium on Tuesday, October 13, maintaining their perfect Champions League start after two matches. Jurrien Timber opened the scoring in the 64th minute, Eberechi Eze added a deflected finish three minutes later and substitute Buk
sports.content: Arsenal scored three times in seven second-half minutes to beat Lille 3-0 at the Emirates Stadium on Tuesday, October 13, maintaining their perfect Champions League start after two matches. Jurrien Timber opened the scoring in the 64th minute, Eberechi Eze added a deflected finish three minutes later and substitute Bukayo Saka completed the scoring in the 71st minute. Arsenal struggled to turn possession into clear chances during a goalless first hour, while Lille’s Ayase Ueda had an early goal ruled out for offside. Mikel Arteta made five changes from the weekend win over Leeds, then brought on Saka, Kai Havertz and Martin Odegaard; all three were involved in the final goal. The result gave Arsenal six points from six and extended their winning streak in the Champions League league phase to 14 matches. Arsenal next visit Bayern Munich on October 21, while Lille host Galatasaray the same day.
